analysis: Reviewed the SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift patch and the docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md update. The code change splits removeCorrupt into removeFile plus a corruptDropped counter increment. removeFile keeps the same performIndexedRemoval path: removeItemIfSafe under the root, then index removal. That path is serialized by removalLock and refused once the store is closed or disowned. In scanOnDisk, a file past its TTL is now removed through removeFile and not counted as corrupt. Files that fail parsing, authentication, metadata or tag checks still go through removeCorrupt. Expired files are still deleted at scan time and never inserted into the index. This does not weaken the TTL bound (30 min, T-041 mitigation b) and does not touch crypto, HMAC naming, epoch handling or the epoch-rotation policy. The `continue` before index.insert and the commitments update means expired files contribute no parent commitments. A delta child whose parent expired is therefore not a candidate and ages out. The doc already describes this, and the scan's existing handling of missing parents is unchanged in this patch. The effect is limited to telemetry: corrupt_drops_total no longer inflates on expiry, which reduces false integrity alarms but could slightly weaken tamper signaling only if an attacker backdates mtime, and that case just causes deletion. The doc edit matches the code and adds no new attack surface. I identified no security regression. Remaining integration questions: whether removal at scan time occurs before the store owns its epoch, and how the unchanged surrounding scanOnDisk code handles the root, which is outside the supplied excerpt.
